title: Meaning and properties of matter
competency: Define matter with examples from day-to-day life.

keywords.def: Anything that has mass and occupies space.
The amount of matter in a sample.
Known by its effect. It cannot be seen, touched, smelt or weighed. Heat, light and sound are energy.

en.text: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space. Plants, water, soil, rocks and even air and bacteria are matter. Heat, light and sound are forms of energy. They have no mass and take no space, so they are not matter.

screens.title: Matter or not?
screens.ask: Which of these is NOT matter?
screens.after: Sound is energy. It has no mass and takes no space. Air, soil and water are all matter.

screens.title: Unit 2 Matter in our surrounding
paras: The objects around us are called matter.
Matter exists in three states: solids, liquids and gases.
Water can be ice (solid), water (liquid) or steam (gas).
The state depends on temperature and pressure.

screens.title: 2.1.1 What is matter?
paras: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space.
Mass is the amount of matter in a sample.
Matter includes living and nonliving things.
Some matter we can see: plants, water, soil, rocks, a table, this book.
Some we cannot see with our eyes: air and bacteria.

screens.title: Energy is not matter
paras: Energy is known by its effect.
It cannot be seen, touched, smelt or weighed.
So heat, light and sound are not matter.

screens.text: Hana weighs a flat football. She pumps it full of air and weighs it again. What happens?
screens.why: The air pumped in is matter. Matter has mass, so the ball gets slightly heavier.
screens.clue: Is the air inside the ball matter?
